title: Animals
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 4 Science and Technology; not yet checked by a CBC Science and Technology teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Use the animals of the school compound first: hens, ants, a goat, earthworms after rain, spiders in a corner. A model backbone (cotton reels on a string) helps the child feel why it bends.

skills.key_step: The child checks an animal (any size, from an ant to a cow) against all the signs of life and does not rely on movement alone.

floor.prerequisite: Can name animals in the locality.
floor.question: Name two animals kept at home.
floor.answer: for example a cow and a hen

representations: live animals in the compound: ants, a hen, a goat
pictures of animals laying eggs and giving birth
a table of signs of life ticked for each animal
steps: List the signs: feed, breathe, move, grow, reproduce, respond, remove waste, die.
Tick the signs for a hen, then for an ant.
Tick the signs for a river or a car: most are missing.
Say: an animal shows all the signs, whatever its size.
contexts: ants carrying food to their hole
a sleeping goat in the shade

board.do: Draw a table: signs of life down the side, hen and river across the top.
Tick every sign for the hen.

board.say: Which signs does a river show?

board.do: Wait for the child to find only movement.

misconceptions.ask: How do new hens come about?
misconceptions.repair: Some animals give birth to live young; others, like hens and fish, lay eggs.

listen_for: it is not moving so it is dead
misconceptions.repair: An animal that rests still breathes and grows: it is alive.

listen_for: an ant is an insect, not an animal
misconceptions.ask: Does an ant feed, move and lay eggs?
misconceptions.repair: Insects, worms and fish are animals too.

listen_for: it moves so it is alive
misconceptions.ask: Does a river eat, breathe or grow babies?
misconceptions.repair: Moving alone does not make a thing alive; check all the signs.

checks.question: Give two signs that show an ant is a living thing.
checks.answer: any two of: it feeds, moves, breathes, grows, lays eggs, responds, dies
checks.shows: signs of life in a small animal

checks.question: A learner says a motorbike is alive because it moves and makes smoke. What is wrong?
checks.answer: It does not grow, feed or reproduce, so it is not alive

skills.key_step: The child asks one question of each animal, "Does it have a backbone?", and sorts it, ignoring legs, size and shells.

floor.prerequisite: Knows that some animals have bones.
floor.question: Does a cow have bones inside its body?

representations: a model backbone made of cotton reels on a string
pictures of a fish skeleton and a snail shell
steps: Feel your own backbone down the middle of your back.
For each animal ask: is there a backbone inside?
Put it in the vertebrate or invertebrate column.
Check the hard cases: snake, fish, hen (vertebrates); crab, snail, spider (invertebrates).
contexts: a snail on the school wall after rain

board.do: Draw two columns: "has a backbone" and "no backbone".
Write snake, crab, hen, spider, tilapia under the table.

board.say: No legs: does it have a backbone?

board.do: Wait for the child to decide.
Ask the child to place the other four.

listen_for: a snake has no legs so no backbone
misconceptions.ask: When you eat fish, what long bone runs down the middle?
misconceptions.repair: Snakes and fish have backbones even with no legs.

listen_for: a spider has legs so it is a vertebrate
misconceptions.ask: If you squash a grasshopper, do you find bones?
misconceptions.repair: Legs do not mean a backbone; insects and spiders have none.

listen_for: the snail's shell is its bone
misconceptions.ask: Is the shell inside or outside the snail?
misconceptions.repair: A backbone is inside the body; a shell is a cover outside.

misconceptions.ask: What did you find in the chicken stew?
misconceptions.repair: Birds have backbones: they are vertebrates.

checks.question: Sort these: tilapia, earthworm. Which is a vertebrate?
Which list holds only invertebrates: (A) crab, spider, snail (B) snake, crab, ant?

skills.key_step: The child gives "it has a backbone" (or "it has no backbone") as the reason, and rejects size, legs, wings, water or softness as rules.

floor.prerequisite: Can sort common animals into the two groups.
floor.question: Is a cow a vertebrate?

representations: odd pairs: a big crab and a small mouse
steps: State the rule: vertebrates have a backbone.
Test a wrong rule on odd pairs (big or small, legs or not).
Show where each wrong rule fails.

board.do: Write the rule "big animals are vertebrates".
Point at a mouse and a big crab.
board.say: Does the rule work for these two?

board.do: Wait for the child to find the mouse breaks it.
Cross out the rule and write "has a backbone".

listen_for: it is small so it is an invertebrate
misconceptions.ask: Is a baby chick a vertebrate?
misconceptions.repair: Size does not decide; a mouse and a chick have backbones.

misconceptions.ask: A butterfly has wings. Does it have a backbone?
misconceptions.repair: Wings and legs are not the rule; only the backbone is.

listen_for: it lives in water so it is a vertebrate
misconceptions.ask: An octopus lives in water. Does it have bones?
misconceptions.repair: Where an animal lives does not tell you about its backbone.

listen_for: it is soft so no backbone
misconceptions.ask: Your skin is soft. Is there a backbone under it?
misconceptions.repair: Soft skin can cover a backbone; ask what is inside.

checks.question: Why is a snake a vertebrate?
A learner says a millipede is a vertebrate because it has many legs. What is the correct reason to use?
checks.answer: Whether it has a backbone: a millipede has none, so it is an invertebrate
